title: Rules, Policies and Subject Change in the Workplace

sections.content:
You know the choice between an infinitive and *que* + subjunctive from B2 Unit 4. In workplace policies, contracts and union discussions, this contrast separates a general institutional goal from an obligation placed on another party.

When the same subject both wants, expects or avoids an action and carries it out, use the infinitive: *La empresa busca evitar los despidos.* Impersonal evaluations without a named agent also take the infinitive: *Conviene revisar la jornada laboral.*

The moment a second subject enters the clause — the staff, management, a union or a contract — Spanish switches to *que* + subjunctive: *La empresa busca que los equipos reduzcan la rotación*, *Conviene que el sindicato revise el convenio*. In formal labour writing, verbs such as *evitar*, *procurar*, *esperar*, *lamentar* and *exigir* follow this split cleanly whenever no indirect object pronoun names the second party.

sections.title: Same subject / general rule vs. second subject
rows: La dirección espera mejorar la conciliación.
La dirección espera que la plantilla mejore la conciliación.
Es necesario regular la contratación temporal.
Es necesario que la ley regule la contratación temporal.

items.spanish: La empresa procura mantener una jornada laboral equilibrada.
items.english: The company tries to maintain a balanced working day.

items.spanish: Los representantes exigen que la dirección respete la negociación colectiva.
items.english: The representatives demand that management respect collective bargaining.

items.spanish: Conviene calcular bien la indemnización antes de firmar el acuerdo.
items.english: It is advisable to calculate the severance pay carefully before signing the agreement.

items.spanish: Conviene que el departamento legal revise las condiciones del despido.
items.english: It is advisable that the legal department review the terms of the dismissal.

sections.content: English uses *for + noun + to + verb* (*It is essential for the union to review the agreement*). Do not translate that word for word with *para* + infinitive after impersonal judgements or verbs of influence: use *que* + subjunctive (*Es esencial que el sindicato revise el acuerdo*). Note also that verbs like *permitir*, *prohibir* and *aconsejar* with an indirect object pronoun (*les permite elegir* / *les permite que elijan*) allow both patterns.
